entry_conditions: The policy can enter during the shared lift-to-carry transition or later in the carry slice when the drawer is already open, the red block is close to the TCP in world coordinates, and the gripper fingers are near the closed carrying width of about 0.018 m per finger. It can also take over partway through the downward/place transition because the causal observation contains the red pose, TCP pose, finger width, pad goal position, and recent one-step motion needed to infer whether the red block is still attached.
exit_conditions: Hand off after the gripper is open near 0.04 m per finger, the red pose is on the outside pad near [-0.18, -0.30, 0.02] m, the red block remains stationary while the TCP has lifted away, and the TCP is retreating toward the blue-block approach side. A geometric red-on-pad condition alone is not the only handoff cue; finger opening and loss of TCP-red co-motion indicate release readiness.
overlap_role: This policy covers the full expanded indices 455:760. It overlaps the predecessor while the red block is already grasped and being lifted into transport, and overlaps the successor after release while the open hand retreats toward the blue-block approach. The overlap is learned from demonstrations, not implemented as a scripted transition.
successor_readiness: The blue approach/grasp/lift successor should receive an open gripper, a red block that is no longer moving with the TCP and is observed on the pad, and a TCP path that has lifted clear of the red object and is moving toward the blue block. The successor should not assume task completion unless the separate global completion contract also observes the drawer open and the blue block inside the drawer.
failure_signatures: Observed failure cues for an inference agent to monitor include the red-TCP offset changing while the fingers remain closed, the red block failing to descend toward the pad, the red block continuing to move with the TCP after finger opening, or a post-release red pose outside the pad region. These are monitoring cues inferred from the heuristic, not hard rejection thresholds or recovery controllers in this policy.
continuation_guidance: Continue this policy while fingers are closed and the red block is being carried toward or down onto the pad, and through the initial opening/lift-away motion until the red pose is stable on the pad. If invoked late with open fingers and stationary red already on the pad, only a short continuation toward the blue-side retreat should be needed before transfer.
limitations: The handoff logic relies on state observations of TCP pose, red pose, finger qpos, and goals. It does not prove contact, does not estimate force, and has not been validated for red slips, loose grasps, or unseen object rotations. The measured indices are support from training data rather than exact deployment thresholds.
